name: Longhole stope drilling
summary: Most ore at the mine comes from longhole stopes: blocks of vein between two drill drifts that are drilled with rings of long holes and then blasted into an opening called a slot. Once technical services releases a stope, the drill drifts are checked and marked up, a production miner sets up a longhole drill, drills the slot and then several hundred metres of ring holes over many shifts, and records every hole. A surveyor and an engineer check the holes against the design and bad holes are redrilled. Stopes are delayed by drill drifts that are not ready, waits for one of three drills, breakdowns, idle time at shift changes and redrills.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine Canadian gold producer running a 500-650 tpd narrow-vein underground mine in northern Ontario on 12-hour shifts and 14-on/14-off rotations, with its own mill.
baseline.notes: Longitudinal longhole stoping in a narrow vein with top-hammer longhole drills; stopes of 2,000-3,500 t; paper drill logs.

trigger: Technical services releases a stope design and drill layout, and the stope is assigned at a shift line-up.
end_state: All rings and the slot are drilled and checked against design, holes are plugged and tagged, and the supervisor has signed the stope off for blasting.

volume.seasonality: None; follows the mine plan and drill availability.

evidence.note: 10,000-19,000 t of ore a month (organisation file demand driver), less development ore, in 2,000-3,500 t stopes gives 4-9 stopes; matches the organisation file entry.
16 production miners on four crews (organisation file), about two drillers per crew-shift; the rest load and blast stopes. Drilling duties per Job Bank.
Release intake, drift checks, per-shift examinations and sign-off.
Ring markup and as-drilled pickup.
As-drilled review.
Drill drift rehabilitation and services.

systems.name: Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)
Shift reports, line-up boards and production tallies (paper and spreadsheets)
Leaky feeder radio and surface radio network
Total stations, cavity monitoring scanner and survey software
Mine design and scheduling software (3D design, scheduling)
Maintenance management system (ERP maintenance module or standalone)

resources.name: Underground utility fleet (scissor lifts and light vehicles)

steps.name: Receive the stope release and drill layout
steps.description: The production supervisor receives the stope release package from technical services: the stope outline, the ring and hole layout with lengths and angles, the slot design and any ground support notes, and files it for the line-up.

evidence.note: Production holes are drilled to a pattern designed by a mining engineer (Wikipedia, Stoping). Releases are issued ahead of drill availability; wait is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Inspect the drill drifts
steps.description: The supervisor walks the top and bottom drill drifts, checking the ground support, scaling, water, power and air services, drainage and muck left on the floor, and decides whether the drill can set up.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854, s. 66: ground examined for dangers before work begins

evidence.note: Ground examination before work (s. 66); share of drifts not ready is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Fix the drill drift
steps.description: A services crew rehabilitates loose ground, extends water, power and air lines, pumps out water or cleans muck so the drill can set up on every ring.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; services work competes with development priorities.

steps.name: Mark up ring lines and hole collars
steps.description: A surveyor sets out the ring lines on the walls and back of the drill drift and marks collar positions and the drill azimuth for each ring from the stope design.

error.defect_description: A ring line set out of position or on the wrong azimuth.

evidence.note: Ring markup by survey is common practice; four surveyors serve all headings and stopes (organisation file).

steps.name: Assign a driller and drill to the stope
steps.description: At line-up the supervisor assigns a longhole driller and one of the three longhole drills to the stope once the drill finishes its current stope or comes back from the shop.

evidence.note: Three longhole drills for 4-9 stopes a month (organisation file); wait is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Do the pre-operational inspection of the drill
steps.description: The driller walks around the longhole drill with the inspection card, checking the feed, rod handler, hoses, brakes, lights and fire suppression, and records defects before use.

error.defect_description: A defect is missed and the drill breaks down during the stope.

control.basis: Company pre-operational (circle check) inspection procedure for mobile equipment

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Tram the drill to the stope
steps.description: The driller trams the drill from its last stope or the shop to the drill drift, giving way to haulage traffic and calling movements on the radio.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Examine and scale the drill site
steps.description: The driller examines the back and walls at the drill site, scales loose rock and fills in the workplace inspection card before setting up.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854, ss. 66 and 67.1: ground examination and scaling before work

evidence.note: Examination and scaling duties; time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Set up on the first ring
steps.description: The driller positions and jacks the drill on the first ring line, connects water, power and air, and aligns the feed to the marked azimuth and dip with the angle indicator.

error.defect_description: Feed aligned at the wrong angle, so holes deviate from design.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Drill the slot raise
steps.description: The driller drills the slot: a tight group of blastholes around larger uncharged reamer holes, or an inverse raise, that will open the first void the stope blasts into.

error.defect_description: Slot holes deviate and converge, risking a frozen slot at blasting.

evidence.note: Every stope needs a slot, often a longhole raise with reamers (Wikipedia); blasts started from a drop or inverse raise at Macassa. Drilling time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the drill to be repaired
steps.description: The supervisor raises a work request and the drill waits for a mechanic to come underground or is trammed to the shop; the driller is moved to other work until it returns.

evidence.note: Breakdown rate and repair wait are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Drill the production rings
steps.description: Over several shifts the driller drills each ring of 64-76 mm holes, typically 10-20 m long, to the lengths and angles on the layout, moving the drill from ring to ring, for a total of roughly 700-1,200 m in a 2,000-3,500 t stope.

error.defect_description: Holes blocked by squeezing ground, short, or deviated beyond tolerance.

evidence.note: Top-hammer rigs drill holes up to about 30 m in a ring pattern (Wikipedia). Metres per stope from 2,000-3,500 t stopes (organisation file) at about 3 t per metre drilled; rate of about 20-30 m per drilling hour is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Hand over the drill at each shift change
steps.description: At every shift change the outgoing driller leaves notes on rings and holes completed and problems, and the incoming driller reads the drill log, re-examines the site and restarts; the drill sits idle over the travel, line-up and blast clearance.

evidence.note: About six of twelve shift hours of equipment movement at conventional mines (CIM Magazine); idle time over 5-10 shift changes is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Record hole depths and problems in the drill log
steps.description: Each shift the driller writes in the drill log the ring and hole numbers, depths drilled, angles, broken ground, water and any hole lost, so the engineer and blaster know which holes are good.

error.defect_description: Depths or lost holes not recorded, so problems surface only when charging.

evidence.note: Organisation file process entry: miners record hole depths and deviations for survey.

steps.name: Supervisor examines the drill site each shift
steps.description: On each shift the supervisor visits the drill, examines the workplace, checks progress against the layout and signs the drill log and workplace card.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854, s. 63(1): supervisor examines every drilling and blasting place each shift

evidence.note: Per-shift examination; total minutes over the drilling shifts are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Survey the as-drilled holes
steps.description: A surveyor picks up the drilled collars and measures hole depths, and with the drill log produces an as-drilled record for the engineer.

evidence.note: Organisation file process entry says hole depths and deviations are recorded for survey; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Engineer compares as-drilled holes with the design
steps.description: The mine engineer overlays the as-drilled holes on the stope design in the planning software, flags holes that are short, blocked or off line, and decides whether to redrill, adjust the loading or redesign part of the stope.

next.condition: squeezed ground or bad holes force a redesign

evidence.note: Organisation file process entry: bad holes or squeezed ground mean redrills that delay the blast and can dilute the stope; shares are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Redrill blocked or deviated holes
steps.description: A driller brings a drill back to redrill or add holes from the redrill list, records them in the drill log and reports completion.

error.defect_description: A redrilled hole is still blocked.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Plug and tag the holes and tram the drill out
steps.description: The driller plugs the hole collars to keep out debris and water, tags the rings with their numbers, cleans up the drill site and trams the drill to its next stope.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Sign off the stope as drilled
steps.description: The supervisor signs the stope off as drilled, sends the final drill log to technical services and tells the blasting crew and engineer that the stope is ready for the loading plan.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Drill drift not ready
exceptions.description: Loose ground, missing services, water or muck must be dealt with before the drill can set up.

exceptions.name: Drill breakdown mid-stope
exceptions.description: The drill waits for repair and the driller moves to other work.

exceptions.name: Redrills
exceptions.description: Blocked, short or deviated holes are redrilled after the engineer's review.

exceptions.name: Stope returned for redesign
exceptions.description: Squeezed ground or many bad holes mean technical services must change the design.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from stope release to stope signed off as drilled
benchmarks.population: Narrow-vein longhole stoping at a 500-650 tpd Ontario mine with three longhole drills

evidence.note: Roughly 4-8 days of drilling over 8-16 shifts plus waits for drift readiness, survey and a free drill; consistent with 4-9 stopes a month on three drills.
Author's estimate at about 3 t broken per metre drilled.

pain_points.description: Released stopes wait for one of three longhole drills to finish its current stope or come back from the shop.

evidence.note: Resource counts from the organisation file.

pain_points.description: The drill stands idle for several hours at every shift change while crews travel, line up and clear for the blast.

evidence.note: About six of twelve shift hours of equipment movement at conventional mines.

pain_points.description: Bad holes are found only after the as-drilled survey and engineer's review, and redrills need the drill brought back.

evidence.note: Organisation file process description.

pain_points.description: Drill logs are handwritten and re-keyed by survey and engineering.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of 2019-2022 practice.

sources.title: Workplace examinations by supervisors (guideline on section 63 of Regulation 854)
sources.publisher: Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development (archived copy in the Library and Archives Canada web archive)
sources.supports: Regulation 854 s. 63(1): a supervisor examines every place where drilling and blasting is being carried out at least once each work shift; s. 63(3): every other place where workers work, in person, at least once each work week; the examination is to identify potential or actual hazards and assess general conditions. The guideline page is dated February 2024; the archive returned a June 2024 capture.

sources.title: Ground control in underground mines
sources.publisher: Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development (archived copy in the Library and Archives Canada web archive)
sources.supports: Regulation 854 s. 6: mine design assessing ground stability prepared under the direction of a professional engineer; s. 6.1: workers kept out of unsupported excavations unless an engineer's written report allows it; s. 66: ground conditions examined for hazards before work begins; s. 67: written procedures for installing ground support; s. 67.1: no other work that hinders scaling; s. 72: records of falls of ground and rockbursts; s. 73: torque and pull tests of rock bolts. Page dated December 2023.

sources.title: Macassa Mine NI 43-101 Technical Report (April 2019), exhibit 99.20
sources.publisher: Kirkland Lake Gold Ltd. (filed on SEC EDGAR)
sources.supports: Comparable Ontario underground gold mine: one hole/one bolt policy with no pre-drilling; bolts on a 1.2 m by 1.2 m dice-five pattern; standard support carried to the working face and screen above 3 m; five ground support classes; longhole stopes for ore dipping about 45 degrees or steeper, drilled from a drilling horizon, with blasts started from a drop or inverse raise; mobile fleet of LHDs, jumbos, bolters and trucks (Table 15-6).

sources.title: Job description: Underground production and development miners (NOC 83100), near Thunder Bay (ON)
sources.supports: Miners set up and operate drills to produce a designated pattern of blast holes, load explosives and detonate them, scale loose rock from walls and roof, drill and install rock bolts, extend air and water pipes, operate LHDs and do routine maintenance; usually more than 40 hours a week.

sources.title: A short solution for the long haul: transitioning from information overload to efficient operation with short interval control
sources.publisher: CIM Magazine (Canadian Institute of Mining, Metallurgy and Petroleum), Peter Braul
sources.supports: Short interval control can be as simple as a radio call every hour or two; in many mines it can take 12 hours for information to reach surface; equipment at a conventional underground mine moves about six hours of a 12-hour shift (against 10 or more at Lac des Iles, Ontario); a Canadian mine found tasks running 100% longer than planned because a jumbo blocked access; a 25-30% productivity gain is thought available at most mines.

sources.title: Stoping
sources.supports: Longhole stoping uses holes drilled by a production drill to a pattern designed by a mining engineer, generally in a radial pattern around the drive; top-hammer rigs are limited to about 30 m hole length; every stope needs a slot (often a longhole raise of tightly spaced blastholes and uncharged reamer holes) to give the initial void; the stope cannot be entered once blasting starts.

assumptions: Stope size of 2,000-3,500 t comes from the organisation file; drilled metres per stope (about 700-1,200 m plus the slot) and drilling rate are the author's estimates.
touch_min of the ring-drilling step adds up the driller's hands-on time across all shifts on the stope; the shift-change step carries the idle time between shifts as a wait.
Steps s13-s15 run during the drilling shifts and are listed after it with concurrent_with set; their minutes are totals across the stope.

Longhole drill hours per stope (about 70 h including repair waits) times 6 stopes is about 420 drill-hours a month, about 40% of the 1,080 available on three drills; the drills also drill cable bolt holes and slots for other work, which is not modelled here.

The organisation file lists prod-miner and ug-shift-supervisor; this file adds surveyor, mine-engineer and ug-services-worker, the inputs survey_data from ts-survey and installed_services from mine-ug-services, and the as-drilled output back to ts-stope-design.

The simulated p90 (about 13 days) is narrower than the benchmark p90 of 20 days because the simulation draws each wait independently, so long waits rarely coincide; in practice a stope that waits for a drill often also waits for drift repairs and survey, which this model does not correlate.
